answer: In limestone country, fog drips from trees into a gauge, and the claimant reports the overnight drip volume, which must track the fog hours the public stations recorded. Bark dark as umber channels the water, a voyage of mist rolls through the valley, and a mesa above the fog stays dry while the trees below drip all night. Faking the volume needs a real foggy hillside per identity, because a copied number cannot match the way drip rates rise and fall with the fog's own rhythm.
